The resolving CPI variant is CPI-W, U.S. city average, all items, series code CWUR0000SA0."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened SSA latest Cost-of-Living Adjustment page to verify formula, latest print, rounding precision, and the 2025 Q3 CPI-W base for the next COLA calculation.","result":"Fetched latest COLA = 2.8 percent; SSA states the Q3 2025 CPI-W average = 317.265, Q3 2024 base average = 308.729, July 2025 CPI-W = 316.349, August 2025 = 317.306, September 2025 = 318.139, and the published calculation was (317.265 - 308.729) / 308.729 x 100 = 2.8 percent."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened SSA COLA history page for the recent official reference class of annual COLA outcomes.","result":"Fetched recent official COLAs: 2016 = 0.3, 2017 = 2.0, 2018 = 2.8, 2019 = 1.6, 2020 = 1.3, 2021 = 5.9, 2022 = 8.7, 2023 = 3.2, 2024 = 2.5, 2025 = 2.8 percent."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened BLS October 2026 release calendar to verify the release date for the September 2026 CPI input that completes Q3 2026 CPI-W.","result":"Fetched official schedule: Consumer Price Index for September 2026 is scheduled on October 14, 2026 at 08:30 AM Eastern; this is the first scheduled release containing the September 2026 CPI-W needed for SSA's 2027 COLA calculation."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened BLS May 2026 CPI Summary for latest CPI-W and inflation momentum before the Q3 measurement window.","result":"Fetched May 2026 CPI-W = 328.829, CPI-W 12-month change = 4.4 percent, CPI-W not-seasonally-adjusted monthly change = 0.7 percent, CPI-U 12-month change = 4.2 percent, core CPI-U 12-month change = 2.9 percent, and energy 12-month change = 23.5 percent."},{"kind":"text","text":"Base rate/reference class: the recent SSA COLA sample averages 3.11 percent over 2016-2025, but it is fat-tailed because pandemic and energy shocks produced 5.9 and 8.7 percent outcomes. A plain outside-view prior is around 3.1 percent, with a wide realized-dispersion interval."},{"kind":"math","text":"Current-input math: using SSA's Q3 2025 CPI-W base average 317.265 and BLS May 2026 CPI-W 328.829 gives (328.829 - 317.265) / 317.265 x 100 = 3.645 percent. I round the point above that to 3.8 percent because Q3 still includes July-September, core inflation is positive, and energy strength may not fully persist."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: model is a 2016-2025 SSA COLA reference-class prior with a May-2026 CPI-W nowcast update; historical sample = [0.3, 2.0, 2.8, 1.6, 1.3, 5.9, 8.7, 3.2, 2.5, 2.8], mean = 3.11, sigma = 2.46 from the values themselves, half-width = 1.28*sigma = 3.14. Adjustment components are level +0.54 from the May CPI-W implied 3.645 percent versus the 3.11 base rate, momentum +0.25 for positive core inflation, one-off energy -0.10 for reversal risk, and policy-mechanism 0.00 because the SSA formula is automatic, giving a 3.8 point. Interval arithmetic: 3.8 - 3.14 = 0.66 and 3.8 + 3.14 = 6.94, rounded to 0.7 to 6.9 percent; this is an approximate normal-reference interval from realized COLA dispersion, not a calibrated backtest."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-consideration: upside risk is another gasoline or tariff-driven Q3 price jump that would land above the interval near or above 7.0 percent. Downside risk is a sharp energy reversal plus soft core readings in July-September that would land below the interval near zero, though the COLA is mechanically floored at 0.0 percent if the rounded CPI-W increase is zero or negative. Outside the interval would also occur if a government shutdown or formal correction changes the first SSA publication timing or label, but the value should still be mechanically determined from CPI-W."},{"kind":"text","text":"Review disposition: accepted the optional reviewer clarifications on approximate interval calibration, strict first-print correction handling, and the mechanical 0.0 percent lower-tail floor; no required fixes were raised."},{"kind":"forecast","point":3.8,"ciLow":0.7,"ciHigh":6.9}]}
